papers.title: Coding4Games: Can Modern Coding Agents Play Modern Video Games?
papers.problem: Game-playing agents that ask a language model at every move cost a lot and react slowly in real-time games.
papers.fix: Coding agents wrote standalone game programs that beat the best screen-based agent on 13 of 15 games.
papers.practicalUseCase: If agents can write their own game bots, you skip a model call at every move, so test them.
papers.limitation: Humans still beat every agent on 10 of the 15 games.

papers.title: PINE: Point, Instance and Normal Estimation in One-Step Diffusion Model
papers.problem: Scene tools use separate models for shape and for objects, which wastes time and compute.
papers.fix: One model predicts 3D points, surface angles, and object masks in one pass, 5.7 times faster than the older pair.
papers.practicalUseCase: If one model does all three jobs, you can drop two models from your pipeline, so try it first.
papers.limitation: The model trained on synthetic images for geometry, so real-world results may differ.

papers.title: LoopDVR: Looped Transformer for Efficient Dense Visual Recognition
papers.problem: Vision models for detection and similar tasks carry too many parameters for small devices.
papers.fix: Reusing blocks across layers cut parameters by about 28% with close accuracy; a 7.0M model scored 50.9 box AP.
papers.practicalUseCase: If layer sharing keeps accuracy, vision models fit smaller hardware, so test it before you shrink models another way.
papers.limitation: The paper reports accuracy that is competitive, not better, than the original models.

papers.title: PartAgent: Agentic 3D Part Segmentation via Expert Integration and Closed-Loop Refinement
papers.problem: Tools that cut 3D objects into parts struggle to combine shape cues with meaning cues.
papers.fix: A training-free agent that checks and fixes its own cuts averaged 69.36 mIoU, 7.28 points above the best rival.
papers.practicalUseCase: If a model can check and repair its own output, quality rises without retraining, so add a review loop.
papers.limitation: It relies on pretrained 3D and 2D expert models, so it inherits their limits.

papers.title: Align the Pair, Not the Sample: Representation Alignment for Faster and Better One-Step Generato
papers.problem: Teams training one-step image generators did not know which training path should receive the alignment loss.
papers.fix: Aligning the paired reconstruction path helped in every test, while aligning the generation path dropped recall from 0.45 to 0.15-0.25.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you train one-step generators, put the alignment loss on the paired path; it needed 2 times fewer priming epochs.
papers.limitation: The evidence comes from ImageNet at 256 pixels, so other image sizes remain untested.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many Muslim-majority countries still have large groups outside formal banking, even as Islamic finance grew.
papers.fix: Across 35 countries from 2005 to 2021, income, schooling, institutions, and internet access shaped inclusion in OIC states.
papers.practicalUseCase: If internet access and schooling drive inclusion, banks and regulators should build digital tools and youth and women programs first.
papers.limitation: It shows links across 35 countries, so it does not prove cause.

papers.title: Examining the Impact of Waqf Literacy on Waqf Behaviour
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Waqf collectors did not know whether better public knowledge of waqf leads Muslims to give more.
papers.fix: Among 642 Indonesian Muslims, waqf literacy raised attitude, social norms, and control, and so raised intention to give.
papers.practicalUseCase: If knowledge of waqf lifts giving, waqf groups should teach donors first, because understanding drives intention before the donation ask.
papers.limitation: It surveys Muslims in Indonesia only, so other countries may differ.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Little was known about how sustainability sukuk grew or what decides the size of each issue.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk issues from 2012 to 2022, equity-based contracts and strong security grew issues; costly second-party opinions shrank them.
papers.practicalUseCase: If second-party opinions cost too much, small issuers stay out, so regulators should cut those costs and favor equity-based contracts.
papers.limitation: It covers 2012 to 2022, and growth sits mostly in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Saudi Arabia.

papers.title: From Clicks to Credit: AI-Measured Halal Product Awareness and Halal Financing Depth across OIC Countries
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Lenders did not know whether public interest in halal products pushes Islamic financing higher.
papers.fix: In 16 OIC countries from 2014 to 2023, more halal searches raised total Islamic financing, mostly through Murabaha and Ijarah.
papers.practicalUseCase: If halal demand pulls financing up, banks should offer simple Murabaha and Ijarah products where halal searches are rising.
papers.limitation: Search volume only approximates awareness, and the effect on Mudarabah and Musharakah is weak.
